title: The Statistical Benefits of Multiple Responses for Learning from Demonstrations
abstract: arXiv:2609.33291v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Many generative systems return multiple candidate responses and are evaluated according to the best one. Recent work shows that, when demonstrations are optimal, pass@$k$ can reduce the sample complexity of learning from demonstrations by a logarithmic factor in $k$. We ask what happens when the demonstrator is not assumed to be optimal. We find that multiple responses provide a qualitatively stronger benefit in this setting. In a finite reward-class model with no reward feedback, moving from pass@$1$ to any pass@$k$ with $k\ge2$ changes the worst-case dependence on target accuracy from $1/\varepsilon^2$ to $1/\varepsilon$, uniformly over demonstrator quality. Under standard evaluation, where an unknown reward is fixed before training, increasing $k$ provides an additional and distinct benefit: the optimal dependence on a reward class of size $N$ improves from $\log N$ to $\log N/\log k$. translated_title: 多候选响应用于从示范中学习的统计优势
translated_abstract: 许多生成式系统会返回多个候选响应，并根据其中最优的一个进行评估。最近的研究表明，当示范为最优时，pass@$k$ 能够将通过示范学习的样本复杂度降低一个 $k$ 的对数因子。我们探讨了当示范者不被假设为最优时会发生什么。我们发现，在这种设定下，多个响应能带来定性上更强的优势。在一个没有奖励反馈的有限奖励类模型中，从 pass@$1$ 转变为任何 $k\ge2$ 的 pass@$k$，会将对目标精度的最坏情况依赖从 $1/\varepsilon^2$ 改善为 $1/\varepsilon$，且该结论在所有示范者质量下均成立。在标准评估设定下（即一个未知奖励在训练前被固定），增大 $k$ 还提供了一个额外的独特好处：对大小为 $N$ 的奖励类的最优依赖从 $\log N$ 改善为 $\log N/\log k$。我们进一步证明这两个效应……
tldr: 当示范者并非最优时，返回多个候选响应（pass@$k$）能带来更强的统计优势——将最坏情况下对目标精度的依赖从 $1/\varepsilon^2$ 改善为 $1/\varepsilon$，并将对奖励类大小的依赖从 $\log N$ 改善为 $\log N/\log k$。
en_tdlr: When the demonstrator is suboptimal, generating multiple responses (pass@$k$) yields a qualitatively stronger statistical benefit: improving worst-case dependence on target accuracy from $1/\varepsilon^2$ to $1/\varepsilon$, and dependence on reward class size from $\log N$ to $\log N/\log k$.
